title: Momentum Module 3 Lesson 1: Direction Rebound Unknown Mass custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A particle $P$ of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ moves horizontally to the right with speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards a fixed vertical barrier. The particle rebounds horizontally from the barrier with speed $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the magnitude of the impulse exerted by the barrier on $P$.

Two particles $A$ and $B$, of masses $0.5\text{ kg}$ and $0.3\text{ kg}$ respectively, move towards each other on a smooth horizontal plane. Particle $A$ has speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and particle $B$ has speed $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. In the collision, particle $B$ is brought to rest. Find the speed and direction of motion of $A$ after the collision.

Particle $P$ of mass $m\text{ kg}$ moves with speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a smooth horizontal track and collides directly with a stationary particle $Q$ of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$. In the collision, particle $P$ rebounds with speed $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and particle $Q$ moves forward with speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the value of $m$.

Two particles $A$ and $B$, of masses $0.6\text{ kg}$ and $0.2\text{ kg}$ respectively, travel towards each other on a smooth horizontal floor. Particle $A$ has speed $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and particle $B$ has speed $7\text{ m s}^{-1}$. In the collision, particle $B$ rebounds with speed $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Find the speed of particle $A$ after the collision.

Particle $X$ of mass $m\text{ kg}$ travels with speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a smooth horizontal surface and collides directly with a stationary particle $Y$ of mass $1.2\text{ kg}$. In the collision, particle $X$ is brought to rest and particle $Y$ moves off with speed $2.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the value of $m$.

A ball of mass $0.15\text{ kg}$ travels horizontally with speed $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards a smooth vertical wall. The ball hits the wall at right angles and rebounds horizontally with speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the magnitude of the impulse exerted by the wall on the ball.

questions.prompt: Particle $A$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ moves with speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along a smooth horizontal surface towards particle $B$ of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$, which is moving towards $A$ with speed $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The particles collide directly. Immediately after the collision, the direction of motion of $B$ is reversed and its speed is $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of $A$ immediately after the collision, and state its direction of motion.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the loss of kinetic energy of the system due to the collision.

questions.prompt: Particle $P$ of mass $m\text{ kg}$ is projected with speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ on a smooth horizontal table towards a stationary particle $Q$ of mass $0.8\text{ kg}$. In the collision, particle $Q$ acquires a speed of $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Given that particle $P$ rebounds with a speed of $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (moving in the opposite direction to its initial motion), find the value of $m$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the magnitude of the impulse exerted by $P$ on $Q$ during the collision.

questions.prompt: Particle $A$ of mass $m\text{ kg}$ is moving on a smooth horizontal surface with speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ when it collides directly with a stationary particle $B$ of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$. Immediately after the collision, $B$ moves with speed $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and the speed of $A$ is $1\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Assuming that particle $A$ continues to move in its original direction after the collision, find the value of $m$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Assuming instead that particle $A$ rebounds so that its direction of motion is reversed after the collision, find the value of $m$, and calculate the loss of kinetic energy in this case.

questions.prompt: Particle $P$ of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ is projected across a smooth horizontal section of a floor with speed $7\text{ m s}^{-1}$ towards particle $Q$ of mass $m\text{ kg}$, which is initially at rest. The particles collide. Immediately after the collision, $P$ rebounds in the opposite direction with speed $1\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and $Q$ moves forward onto a rough horizontal section of the floor where the coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.32$. Particle $Q$ slides a distance of $2.5\text{ m}$ on the rough floor before coming to rest. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the speed of $Q$ immediately after the collision is $4.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the mass $m$ of particle $Q$, and find the magnitude of the impulse exerted by $P$ on $Q$.

questions.prompt: Two particles $A$ and $B$, of masses $0.2\text{ kg}$ and $0.6\text{ kg}$ respectively, lie on a smooth horizontal table between two fixed vertical barriers. Particle $A$ moves towards $B$ with speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ while $B$ is initially at rest. In the collision, $A$ rebounds with speed $1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of $B$ immediately after the collision, and show that the impulse exerted on $A$ has magnitude $1.5\text{ N s}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Particle $B$ subsequently strikes a smooth vertical barrier ahead of it and rebounds with half of its speed. Find the speed of $B$ after rebounding from the barrier, and determine whether $B$ can catch up with $A$.

questions.prompt: Particle $A$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ moves with speed $u\text{ m s}^{-1}$ on a smooth horizontal table towards a stationary particle $B$ of mass $m\text{ kg}$. In the direct collision, particle $A$ rebounds with speed $\frac{1}{5}u$ and particle $B$ acquires a forward speed $v_B$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that $v_B = \frac{3u}{5m}$, and find the impulse exerted by $A$ on $B$ in terms of $u$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that particle $B$ subsequently collides directly with a stationary particle $C$ of mass $0.9\text{ kg}$ and coalesces with it to move with speed $\frac{1}{3}v_B$, find the value of $m$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Using $m = 0.45\text{ kg}$, find the speed $v_B$ in terms of $u$, and find the ratio of the final speed of the combined particle $BC$ to the original speed $u$ of particle $A$.

questions.prompt: A particle $A$ of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$ is released from rest at a point on a smooth plane inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\alpha = 0.2$. Particle $A$ slides a distance of $2.25\text{ m}$ down the plane and strikes a stationary particle $B$ of mass $m\text{ kg}$. Immediately after the collision, particle $A$ rebounds and travels back up the plane with speed $1.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, while particle $B$ moves down the plane with speed $1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the acceleration of $A$ down the plane, show that its speed immediately before impact is $3.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and calculate the distance up the plane that $A$ travels after rebounding before coming to instantaneous rest.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the mass $m$ of particle $B$, and find the total kinetic energy lost by the two particles during the collision.
